Note::NlpAccessor::overlap_citations¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::overlap_citations(const Note& other) const

Citation-Set Containment Score Between Two Notes¶

overlap_citations(other) scores each cell pair by the overlap coefficient of their citation-marker sets and returns a shape-preserving Float64 Note of native scores. It is the citation-set containment member of the set-similarity family; see also jaccard_citations and intersect_citations.

How the score is computed¶

A citation marker is a bracketed number ([1], [42], one to three digits) or an author–year group ((Smith, 2020), (Lee, 2021a)). Markers keep their brackets, are lowercased, and are deduplicated into sets A and B. The score is |A ∩ B| / min(|A|, |B|), in [0, 1], symmetric — 1.0 when the smaller reference list is contained in the larger.

A cell with no bracket-or-paren and digit has an empty set. Both sets empty → 1.0; one empty and one not → 0.0. The default printer shows up to six decimals, trailing zeros trimmed.

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

Per cell and pairwise; equal numel or a scalar (numel() == 1) broadcast. Bytes-mode input raises Note::NlpAccessor::overlap_citations requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes) (or rhs); a numel mismatch raises Note::NlpAccessor::overlap_citations expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

Example 1: One Reference List Inside Another¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"[1] [2]"})
                 .nlp().overlap_citations(pluss::make_note({"[1] [2] [3] [4]"}))
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, dtype=Float64)
[1]

{[1], [2]} is a subset of {[1], [2], [3], [4]} → 1.0. jaccard_citations here would give 2/4 = 0.5.
